bib.title: E-Commerce Bench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Business Operation

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: Extracted all 64 PDF pages (243,952 chars). Read in full: abstract, intro, related work, section 3 metric definitions (3.7), sections 4 and 5, and Table 2. Skimmed: references, and appendices A-H (harness, data, kernel, metric formulas, per-dimension tables, case studies, prompts), which I only located by their contents list. There is no limitations section. The Table 2 text extraction merges some adjacent cells, so I cross-checked it against the prose.

SOURCE: "E-Commerce Bench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Autonomous Business Operation". First author Wei Fan (equal contribution with Xinjie Shen; done during a summer internship). Affiliations: Qwen Team, Alibaba Group; Taobao & Tmall Group; HKUST CSE (Fan and Yangqiu Song). Dated 2026-09-01 (arXiv 2608.30730v1, cs.LG, 31 Aug 2026). No venue is stated, so preprint. Code: github.com/QwenLM/E-CommerceBench. The authors are the Qwen team, and their own Qwen3.8-Max-Preview is the top open-weight model.

CORE CLAIM: This is an open-source benchmark where an agent runs up to 4 online stores for a simulated 365 days. Both market sides are deterministic: a fixed demand model for customers, and a rule-based negotiation kernel for suppliers, with an LLM only rewording the replies. Because of that, outcome differences belong to the agent and not to sampling noise. The authors report that no model leads on all seven axes (profit plus six diagnostics), so a single total-assets number hides weaknesses.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (setup for all: 18 models, 8 proprietary and 10 open-weight, 5 independent episodes each = 90 episodes, one fixed world, 18 shared tools, provider default settings with thinking forced on where available, 4,000-turn cap, ¥100,000 start. Metric is end-of-year total assets from bank, wallet and escrow. Grading is by the simulator, not an LLM. Bankrupt runs stay pooled into every mean.)
1. GPT-5.6 Sol (max) mean ¥1,431,425 (std ¥314k; abstract and Table 2). Qwen3.5-Plus mean ¥1.1k. The paper says a "factor of 1,264" separates top from bottom. Qwen3.8-Max-Preview mean ¥416k (std 111), ¥416,252 in the abstract, "38% above GLM 5.2 (high)" (¥301k).
2. Bankruptcy: 10 of 90 episodes went bankrupt, all in four models: GPT-5.5 2/5, Claude Opus 4.6 2/5, Gemini 3.1 Pro 2/5, Qwen3.5-Plus 4/5. Bankruptcy is the tenth consecutive negative bank day. Two GPT-5.5 episodes failed on day 17, before any revenue settled.
3. Fraud: GPT-5.6 Sol has BadSpend% 18.48 (16th of 18); Claude Opus 4.7 has 0.12 (best). The share of approaches that became orders runs from 4.0% (Opus 4.7) to 31.7% (GPT-5.6 Sol). Defective lots are 53.4% of money reaching fraudulent suppliers. The standard deviation of the share exceeds its mean for 15 of 18 models, so the rankings are noisy.
4. Efficiency: Fable5 earns ¥479 profit per tool call against GPT-5.6 Sol's ¥363, on 59.9% fewer calls. Across all 18 models, 71.8% of calls go to shipping, advancing the day, withdrawing and publishing, and only 0.66% of calls revise prices.
5. Learning: AnchorRatio (1.0 equals a random ordering of the agent's own prices; lower is better) is 0.834 for Qwen3.8-Max-Preview and 0.918 for Gemini 3.5 Flash. The field median is 1.369 and Qwen3.5-Plus is 1.860. Fifteen models miss their permutation null by more than 2 standard deviations in the expensive direction. The intro cites 8,647 repeat purchases; 16 of 18 models show no clear price decline. Negotiation (CSE+): best 0.811 (Opus 4.7), worst 0.596 (Kimi K2.6), and accepting the opening quote scores 0.50.

QUOTES:
- "Ordering by assets recovers only part of the skill behind it" (p.16).
- "Failure patterns spread across the whole field rather than concentrating in the weakest models. Every model trips at least five rules, Gemini 3.1 Pro all ten, and tripping fewer of them does not make a model richer." (p.20)

LIMITS: Each model has only 5 episodes in one fixed world, and the authors flag this as a small sample. The environment is deterministic, so a result on one world may not transfer, and it is a synthetic simulator with a fixed demand model. The supplier-dialogue renderer is an LLM, so wording varies between runs. The model tiers were assigned by the authors. No cost or latency is scored (the paper says "the score stays blind to it"). The paper cannot tell apart three explanations for no learning (context eviction, an unused memory store, no in-episode gradient) and says "the evaluation separates none of them". The Qwen team wrote it and its own model leads the open-weight tier. Model names and versions are as printed (GPT-5.6 Sol, Fable5 and others). There is no human baseline and no check of simulator realism against real sellers that I saw. I did not read the appendices closely, so I cannot say whether they cover this.

BUILDS ON: Vending-Bench (Backlund & Petersson 2025) and Vending-Bench 2 (Andon Labs 2026). YC-Bench (He et al. 2026). MerchantBench (Shi et al. 2026) and RetailBench (Zhang et al. 2026c), which have real data but no negotiation or adversarial suppliers. TERMS-Bench (Zhang et al. 2026a), whose negotiation-partner design the kernel extends. Memory design from Packer et al. 2024 and Park et al. 2023. Metric and statistics practice from Kapoor et al. 2025 ("AI agents that matter") and Miller 2024. The anchoring-bias reading cites Lou & Sun 2026.

BEST-FIT NOTE SECTION: The note has no MerchantBench mention (grep found none), only τ-bench. Best fit is "Agent-specific suites", as a new continuing-task or business-simulation paragraph beside the MedBrowseComp and NatureBench paragraphs. A secondary fit is "Non-determinism: run every task k times", because it deterministically removes counterpart noise yet still uses only 5 runs. The note lacks three things this paper covers. First, a continuing-task benchmark with no terminal state that scores accumulated outcome. Second, a deterministic scripted counterpart (the kernel) with an LLM used only for wording. Third, a multi-axis capability profile showing the best earner is not the best negotiator, with fraud measured by cash flow ("follows the cash") instead of refusals. Also the repeated-purchase learning test (AnchorRatio against a permutation null), and rule-based failure detectors.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 2 (p.2), the 7-axis radar for the strongest model per vendor family. Figure 9 (p.17) gives the same profiles for 6 models with ranks, e.g. GPT-5.6 Sol "rank 1·7·16·9·2·17·4". Figure 1 (p.2) shows mean assets as a multiple of the stake with bankruptcies marked.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table 2 extraction fuses some cells (for example "4790.22" is 479 and 0.22), so I read the values with that in mind. Fan's affiliations are stated per author; the equal-contribution note covers Fan and Shen.
